A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VSLS research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original VSLS keyframe-retrieval, computational-efficiency, and video-QA results in Tables 1–4, supplemented by case and iteration analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports query-relation coverage and a hyperparameter-search finding.

M1.justification: The four relation-verification rules, adaptive sampling, confidence updates, stopping procedure, and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same method. Newly specified hyperparameter values document the existing framework rather than establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LONGVIDEOBENCH, VIDEO-MME, HAYSTACK-LVBENCH, and HAYSTACK-EGO4D for the same keyframe-search and video-QA tasks. The added relation-coverage analysis uses existing datasets without introducing a distinct task or test environment.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain uniform sampling, VIDEOAGENT, retrieval-based methods, T* variants, and the same QA-model comparators. v1 Tables 2 and 3 become v2 Tables 3 and 2 without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: v2 newly reports a hyperparameter-search protocol over alpha values 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, and 1.0, and changes relation-frequency reporting to average occurrences per question. Existing benchmark metrics, model configurations, and frame budgets remain unchanged; the newly disclosed thresholds do not establish changed settings or reruns of earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Section 4.1 adds an analysis of whether every query maps to at least one relation category, and Section 2.3.3 briefly reports hyperparameter-search findings. The relation-type comparison, frame-count study, handwriting case study, and iteration analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for the main results. v2 checklist item 7 explicitly acknowledges the existing point-estimate reporting practice without adding uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the four matched benchmark tables remain unchanged. Figure 4 replaces percentage distributions with per-question means, including 1.20 spatial relations for LONGVIDEOBENCH and 1.75 for VIDEO-MME. v2 also newly reports universal query mapping and alpha=0.3 with gamma=0.5 as the best parameter choice.

T1.justification: The task definitions, algorithmic equations, appendix formulations, and complexity arguments retain their mathematical substance. New Appendix A provides conceptual linguistic and logical motivation, without introducing a formal theorem, proof, or guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: four-relation semantic-logical search, approximately 1.4% frame sampling, improved retrieval and QA, and plug-and-play integration. The claimed 8.7% GPT-4O improvement is unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A expands the rationale for the four categories, while Section 4.1 interprets universal query mapping as supporting their completeness. New Appendix I identifies latency constraints and detector failures under poor lighting, occlusion, or unusual viewpoints; Appendix J discusses inherited detector biases.

D1.justification: v2 specifies tau=0.5, alpha=0.3, gamma=0.5, and identifies five frames as the experimental temporal threshold. Appendix E.6 adds CPU, memory, A800 GPU, Python, PyTorch, and NCCL specifications absent from v1. Both PDFs continue to promise a future code release.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused grounding in case grammar, cognitive semantics, discourse theory, and knowledge representation, with references including Fillmore, Talmy, Mann and Thompson, and Sowa. It removes the fMRI-reconstruction survey citation, while retaining its positioning against existing video-search approaches.

P1.justification: The introduction and substantial portions of the method exposition, metric explanations, QA discussion, and complexity analysis are rewritten or condensed. Distribution Update is nested under Section 2.3, appendix headings are reorganized, and author-year citations replace numbered citations.

P2.justification: The document changes from a predominantly two-column layout to a single-column format, extensively relocating and resizing existing displays. Relation definitions become a four-panel display, Tables 2 and 3 exchange numbering and placement, and Figure 4 changes from percentage pie charts to grouped bars with a per-question axis.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through previously missing parameter values and computing specifications, and adds concrete latency and detector limitations. These are useful, bounded gains while the benchmark evidence remains unchanged. The new coverage analysis supports applicability, although assigning a relation to every query does not establish semantic completeness; this qualification limits the strength of the added interpretation.
